analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + HF Update, Midterms Europe Conviction List Alstom Ryanair LVMH Nicotine 2 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities finished the week lower: SPX -182 bps to 7580, NDX -346 bps to 28384 (about a 7% move in October), RTY -166 bps to 2811. Nasdaq had its worst session since June and second-worst YTD, with the Tech sector -4.24%.

The AI trade took the biggest hit: the GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) fell 8.25% on the week and the GS Data Center basket (GSTMTDAT) fell 7.35%. In Europe, EU High Beta Momentum (GSPEMOMO) fell 2.8% and EU Beta (GSP3BETA) fell 2.5%, while the EU Stagflation pair (GSPESTAG) rose 2% and was among the best performing baskets.

October cross-asset moves: NDX vs. Equal Weight S&P had its worst month since 2002, the SOX broke below its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025, and Software vs. Semis had its second-best month in 10 years. AI vs. 'AI at Risk' had its second-worst month since the launch of ChatGPT, while S&P ex-AI had its strongest month (+7.64%) over the same period.

Hedge fund performance: Fundamental LS managers were up 0.3% on the week (alpha +0.1%), with Monday-Thursday gains partly erased by Friday. Alpha came from stock selection and Health Care, partly offset by Brazil exposure. Communication Services and Info Tech were the most net bought sectors, with Info Tech net bought for the first time in 5 weeks. North America was the only net bought region.
For October, Fundamental LS managers were down 3.5% (alpha -1.8%). YTD they are up 9.1% (alpha +6.6%).

Flow: Asset managers finished net sellers (reversing early-week tech demand and more) while hedge fund flows finished balanced. Supply was concentrated in tech but was orderly compared with the prior ~2 weeks. The moves looked systematic / top-down driven, with ETFs at ~31% of the tape (highest full-session level since June), plus month-end effects.

In a Democratic sweep scenario, GS's favorite long basket is Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA). Democrats have pushed to revive the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025, and reauthorizing them should improve earnings for hospitals, outpatient providers and health insurers facing rising bad debt and uncompensated care costs.

US Midterms: prediction markets imply more than 90% odds that Democrats win the House and more than 65% that they win the Senate. Fiscal deadlines (spending authority extension, debt limit increase) would be the main legislative focus under a Democratic majority. GS does not expect major fiscal policy changes over the next 2 years but sees spending potentially rising.
Europe Conviction List: Deutsche Bank and Carlsberg are added, HSBC, Haleon and CTP are removed.

US Strategy: Q3 2026 earnings show strong growth that is no longer accelerating. Analysts continued to raise forward earnings estimates, but the pace of upward revisions has slowed. Q3 results support GS's view that AI capex will keep growing but that its growth rate is peaking.

Alstom cut 2026 guidance: sales growth to low-to-mid single digits (vs 5% previously), adjusted EBIT margin to 1% (vs 6.5%), FCF to -1.5bn (vs positive). The cut is primarily due to Coradia Max milestones slipping into later years, and also to prolonged uncertainty in the Middle East. The company says the Coradia Max issues were first identified in Q1.

Ryanair: initial read on results is ok. Q2 PAT was in line and Q3 fares are trending modestly higher y/y. A new EUR800m share buyback starting in February signals confidence. Fuel hedging for FY28 is only 25% (up from 15%), which is a headwind into next year.

Europe nicotine: GS upgrades BAT to Buy (22% upside) and keeps Imperial at Buy (22% upside). Both offer double-digit total returns backed by earnings growth, rising capital returns and ~6% dividend yields. Into FY27, GS sees nicotine's defensive qualities and margins as attractive amid consumer and input cost uncertainty.

LVMH (Buy, PT EUR495, 25% upside): GS argues the shift from a commercial, fashion-driven brand to a more institutional, handbag and accessories strategy centered on the 'art of travel' has weighed on sales over the past 12 months and should be a much smaller headwind in 2027. GS also sees gradual sales improvement at Dior.
Unilever: GS published 10 investor debates ahead of the Unilever capital markets day (CMD).

Positioning in Mag7 has been very resilient despite the volatile TMT tape, moving from under-owned in June to near YTD highs in exposure. GS expects the group to remain a source of funds, limiting near-term dip-buying demand.
HF pain: the GS HF VIP vs VIP Short had its 3rd-worst month in the past 15 years. GS says P&L protection over P&L generation will limit offense in the near term (buyers live higher).
